page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It lacks local storage and has no integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2166.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.34 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show relative limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 3990.58 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 26.13 GB/sec fall into the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth measured at 36.73 GB/sec. Despite these multi-threaded bottlenecks, the server maintains average performance in database operations, static web serving, and small-scale LLM inference.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4s_v6 offers a balanced resource profile for workloads that prioritize single-core speed over massive parallelization or high memory throughput. Because it lacks local storage, users must rely on external Premium Storage, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as lightweight web serving, text processing, and basic database operations that do not require high-density local disk I/O or massive memory bandwidth.
